question: Which of the following terms is used for the flat circular (stone-disk) structure at the top of North Indian temple architecture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amalaka (Amalaka)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amalaka (Amalaka):**
 
• The Amalaka is a disc-shaped stone structure that sits at the apex of the Shikhara in North Indian temple architecture.
 
• It is a ribbed or fluted stone disk, typically circular in shape.
 
• It serves as a platform for the Kalash.
 
• The Amalaka is a significant architectural element, symbolizing the transition from the earthly realm to the divine.
 
• It is a distinctive feature of Nagara style temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shikhara:**
 
• The Shikhara is the towering, mountain-like spire that rises above the Garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum) in North Indian temples.
 
• It is a prominent feature of Nagara style architecture.
 
• Shikharas can vary in shape and size, depending on the region and the temple's style.
 
• It represents the mountain peak, and is seen as the home of the gods.
 
• It is a very important part of the temple structure.
 
• **Kalash:**
 
• The Kalash is a pot-shaped finial that sits atop the Amalaka.
 
• It is often made of metal, such as copper or brass.
 
• The Kalash is considered a symbol of auspiciousness and abundance.
 
• It often has a coconut and mango leaves placed within it.
 
• It is the very top most part of the temple.
 
• **Interval:**
 
• "Interval" is not a specific architectural term related to North Indian temple structures.
 
• It is a general term referring to a space or gap between objects.
 
• It does not refer to a architectural element of a temple.
 
• It is a general term.
 
• It is not related to temple architecture.
